statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of triples of indices (i,j,k) such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(arr), |arr[i] - arr[j]| <= a, |arr[j] - arr[k]| <= b, and |arr[i] - arr[k]| <= c. Distinct index triples are counted separately even when their corresponding array values are equal.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: The function does not fail: there exists an I64 value r such that count_good_triplets arr a b c returns r.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and 0 <= r <= C(len(arr),3), where C(n,3) = n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6 is the number of index triples 0 <= i < j < k < n.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1 exactly when |arr[0] - arr[1]| <= a, |arr[1] - arr[2]| <= b, and |arr[0] - arr[2]| <= c; otherwise r = 0.
preconditions: len(arr) = 3, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(arr)*(len(arr)-1)*(len(arr)-2)/6.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, there is an integer v such that arr[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= v <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: For every integer v, let f(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(arr) and arr[i] = v. The function returns a result r, and r = sum over all integers v of f(v)*(f(v)-1)*(f(v)-2)/6.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and a = 0, b = 0, c = 0.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of triples of indices (i,j,k) such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(arr), |arr[i] - arr[j]| <= a, and |arr[j] - arr[k]| <= b.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, and c = 1000.

statement: If count_good_triplets arr a1 b1 c1 returns r1 and count_good_triplets arr a2 b2 c2 returns r2, then r1 <= r2.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and each of a1,b1,c1,a2,b2,c2 lies in [0,1000], with a1 <= a2, b1 <= b2, and c1 <= c2.

statement: The function returns results r and s for (arr,a,b,c) and (arr2,a,b,c) respectively, and r = s.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000, arr2 has the same length as arr, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr2[i] <= 1000, and there exists an integer t such that arr2[i] = arr[i] + t for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr).

statement: The function returns r for (arr,a,b,c) and s for (arr2,b,a,c), and r = s.
preconditions: len(arr) = n with 3 <= n <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000, arr2 has length n, and arr2[i] = arr[n-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r > 0 if and only if there exist indices i,j,k such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(arr), |arr[i] - arr[j]| <= a, |arr[j] - arr[k]| <= b, and |arr[i] - arr[k]| <= c; equivalently, r = 0 exactly when no such index triple exists.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.

statement: Let M be the number of triples of indices (i,j,k) such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(arr), |arr[i] - arr[j]| <= a, and |arr[j] - arr[k]| <= b. The function returns a result r, and r <= M.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3, len(arr) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr) we have 0 <= arr[i] <= 1000, and 0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000, 0 <= c <= 1000.
